correctness.rationale: A connected generalized-quadrangle incidence graph has girth eight, diameter four and cycle rank (st)^2. The scale-two square clique complex has exact full closed-star facets, and descending-size free-face collapses preserve exactly the original graph. At scale three all cross-type distances are <=3 while homogeneous edges encode collinearity; the complex equals X*Y. Stellar subdivision then free-face collapse shows X and Y each have homotopy type of the incidence graph. Join/smash/suspension gives a wedge of (st)^4 3-spheres. The graph metric changes only at integer scales; relative collapse at scale two proves the H1 persistence map is an isomorphism. Exact finite replay checks all proposed collapses, factors and distances for orders 2 and 3; symbolic arguments prove all existing thick orders.

value.rationale: A complete homotopy and positive-degree barcode formula for every finite thick generalized quadrangle is a natural incidence-geometric classification, not a parameter-sliced recomputation. The new scale-three join produces third-dimensional homology of multiplicity (st)^4 after first-dimensional homology of rank (st)^2, and provides useful structural insight beyond the known high-girth square-graph collapse. Its all-order statement and persistence maps are mathematically motivated and not consequences of point/line enumeration alone.
